result.title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
result.summary: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka--Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators show improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including inference in large systems and identification under partial observations or unknown topology, alongside substantial computational savings in coefficient fitting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MAS-PINN：用共享时序特征加个体系数表示多智能体轨迹，交替学习特征、拟合耦合轨迹并估计物理参数，并借助局部交互的无矩阵更新降低仿真与参数辨识的计算和内存开销。
